title: Accessibility
summary: Screen readers on both platforms, accessibility props for roles, labels and state, touch target size, font scaling and reduced motion.

sections.title: Screen readers
sections.body: iOS has VoiceOver and Android has TalkBack. Both read the accessibility tree that React Native builds from your components. Interactive elements need an accessible name and a role, and grouped content should be read as one element where it makes sense.

sections.title: The props
sections.body:
- `accessible`: groups children into one focusable element (`Pressable` and `Text` are accessible by default).
- `accessibilityLabel`: the name read out, needed for icon-only buttons.
- `accessibilityRole` (or the newer `role`): `button`, `link`, `header`, `image`, `switch` and more.
- `accessibilityState`: `{ disabled, selected, checked, busy, expanded }`.
- `accessibilityHint`: what happens when activated, read after a pause.
- `accessibilityLiveRegion` (Android) and `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` for announcing changes.
- `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` (Android) and `accessibilityElementsHidden` (iOS) hide decorative content.
sections.code:
<Pressable
  onPress={toggle}
  accessibilityRole="switch"
  accessibilityLabel="Dark mode"
  accessibilityState={{ checked: dark }}
  hitSlop={8}
>
  <MoonIcon />
</Pressable>

sections.title: Size, text and motion
sections.body:
Touch targets should be at least 44×44 points on iOS and 48×48 dp on Android. Use `hitSlop` to enlarge a small visual target. Text scales with the system font size by default; design layouts that wrap rather than truncate, and cap scaling with `maxFontSizeMultiplier` only where a layout truly cannot grow. Check `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` and tone down large animations.

Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store. The exercise audits a tree of component descriptions for missing labels, roles and small targets.

gotchas.question: A heart icon button toggles favourite. What does it need?
gotchas.answer: `accessibilityRole="button"` (or a toggle role), an `accessibilityLabel` such as "Favourite", and `accessibilityState={{ selected }}` so the state is read out.

gotchas.question: What is the minimum touch target on Android?
gotchas.answer: 48×48 dp per the platform guidelines (44×44 points on iOS).

gotchas.question: A decorative image is read as "image". How do you hide it?
gotchas.answer: Mark it not accessible: `accessible={false}` plus `importantForAccessibility="no"` on Android, or wrap and hide it with `accessibilityElementsHidden` on iOS.
